source.title: Retain-Neutral Surrogates for Min-Max Unlearning
source.authors: Jun-Hao Cai; Dohun Kim; Dowon Kim; Sungjin Choi; Chengjun Jin; Juhyun Park; Changhee Joo

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates a different unlearning method and reports targeted-knowledge and general-ability outcomes relevant to the pre-attack efficacy portion of version A. It does not evaluate recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The WMDP table reports post-unlearning hazardous-domain accuracy and MMLU for ROSU and comparator methods. These bear on unlearning efficacy and retained general ability, but the study does not run the recovery attacks in versions B–E. The table's composite ∆Score is not separately extracted because the component accuracy measures are more directly relevant.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It proposes ROSU, a min–max unlearning optimizer, and reports only post-unlearning WMDP-Bio, WMDP-Cyber and MMLU accuracies for ROSU and comparators (Table 3). It runs no recovery attack of any kind: no relearning, activation ablation, quantization, rephrasing or jailbreak. Version A is what the shallow-unlearning claim challenges, and its contested part is that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge. Near-chance accuracy straight after unlearning is the method's own benchmark performance and cannot show whether the knowledge was removed or only hidden. The paper itself calls ROSU a local first-order guarantee, not a deletion certificate, and says it should complement extraction audits. WMDP and RMU are used as benchmark and baseline tools only.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as far as it goes. The authors conclude that ROSU improves the forgetting–retention trade-off, with the clearest gains in high-coupling regimes, and stays competitive elsewhere. They also say ROSU gives a local first-order surrogate guarantee, not a deletion certificate, and should complement extraction and reconstruction audits.
record.recipe_differences: ROSU uses a retain-orthogonal inner perturbation in min–max unlearning, with a transported outer update and retain-neutral amplification. The study does not implement or evaluate the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that ROSU's gains are clearest in high-coupling settings. Its WMDP setup restricts trainable parameters to MLP down-projection matrices in layers 5–7 and defines objectives at layer 7.
record.problems: The study does not perform any recovery-attack tests, so its results cannot determine whether the reported unlearning is robust to relearning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting. The WMDP table reports no uncertainty values. The paper states that some baseline results are taken directly from UAM due to reproducibility constraints.
record.rows_left_out: TOFU scores in Table 3 and the vision results in Tables 1, 2, and 4 were not extracted: they do not report the targeted-knowledge accuracy and general-ability pair used here to assess the tested portion of version A in the WMDP setup.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge after unlearning. Only accuracy straight after unlearning was measured.
Activation-direction ablation, or analysis of whether the method blocks access rather than deletes.
Low-bit quantization of the unlearned weights.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages or in-context information.
ROSU is not claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with supports labels overstates the study. Near-chance WMDP accuracy after unlearning is exactly the surface result the shallow-unlearning claim says can be misleading, so without any attack it neither supports nor challenges version A. WMDP uses a representation-level variant that edits only down_proj matrices in layers 5–7, following the RMU/UAM setup. The text cites relearning-robust unlearning work and reconstruction attacks, but runs neither.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether simple attacks recover the targeted knowledge after unlearning.
Activation-direction ablation or evidence that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Recovery through prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.
